envelope.text: The typesupport parameter keeps OUR type for the reason RFC-0089 settled

why:
see `c:client_init_default`.

phase-428 Q1 (2026-09-06) — refuse-loud -> adopt-bounded. `rclc_service_init_default` EXISTS at rclc's arity (`packages/api/nros-c/src/service.rs:325`: service, node, type, name) and the correlator files it `same`; the old row promised a refusal nothing emits.

WHAT THE COMPILER POINTS AT: argument 3. rclc takes `const rosidl_service_type_support_t*` and a ported file passes `ROSIDL_GET_SRV_TYPE_SUPPORT(pkg, srv, Name)`; ours takes `const struct rclc_service_type_t*` (the generated `<name>_type` descriptor, e.g. `&add_two_ints_type` in `examples/threadx-linux/c/service-server/src/main.c:138`). An rcl typesupport pointer at that position is an incompatible-pointer diagnostic on the call, naming both types. That is a mechanical edit, not a message with the migration attached, which is why this is adopt-bounded and not refuse-loud.

THE ENVELOPE: the callback is not on this call in either library — rclc supplies it at `rclc_executor_add_service`, ours at `rclc_executor_add_service_raw` (`packages/api/nros-c/include/rclc/detail/nros_generated.h:4942`), so that half ports one-for-one. The service-name expansion caveat in `c:publisher_init` does not apply: services reach `resolve_entity_name` at registration.
